title: Embedding endpoint: adaptive signal routing and slowpath plumbing to reduce tail latency
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Problem: Our embeddings endpoint exhibits intermittent long-tail latency spikes (p99 and above) under mixed-tenancy workloads. Root causes observed in preliminary traces include: (1) requests routed to a slowpath code path due to cache-miss fingerprints, (2) suboptimal kernel selection for specific sequence-length mixes, and (3) microbursting at ingress that forces uneven micro-batch formation.

Goal: Reduce embedding p99 by 20-40% and reduce p95->p99 gap by half for the next month of production traffic without regressions to p50/p90 and without increasing per-token cost by more than 3%. Deliver production-safe mitigations and an automated canary for rollout to Dedicated and Hosted fleets.

Scope: This ticket covers backend changes: adaptive signal routing (real-time decision layer that tags requests to fastpath/slowpath), a "slowpath plumbing" cleanup to limit contention and queue head-of-line blocking, and lightweight kernel hinting based on dynamic sequence-length telemetry. It also defines an experiment harness and metrics for measuring impact. Client-side SDK changes are out of scope and will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for embeddings endpoint decreased by >=20% on production-like mixed-tenancy workload in the experiment cluster
p95->p99 gap reduced by >=50% during load tests that include microbursts and long sequences
no >3% increase in per-token cost observed on the experiment fleet
feature gated with rollout flags and automatic fallback to current routing within 2 minutes of error rate increase
observability: new dashboards (latency quantiles by tenant fingerprint, routing decision breakdown, kernel hint hit rate) available in Console
postmortem checklist and rollback instructions documented in ticket comments
technical_approach:
1) Adaptive signal router: add a lightweight decision stage in ingress that uses short-lived fingerprints (sequence length, tenant slot, recent KV-hits) to choose fastpath vs experimental slowpath variants. The router will maintain an exponentially-weighted moving average of per-fingerprint latency to avoid noisy decisions.

2) Slowpath plumbing: refactor slowpath to remove a global mutex that can be contended under macro-bursts. Replace with per-shard token queues and cooperative draining; add backpressure tokens so slowpath cannot starve fastpath batches.

3) Kernel hinting: emit kernel-hint metadata from the router to downstream executor; hints are best-effort and do not change functional behavior. Implement a fallback probe that tries alternative kernels for a subset of traffic (1-5%) and records latency and correctness.

4) Canary + telemetry: traffic-split control by tenant tag; capture quantile deltas and tail event traces; build a canary gate that auto-rolls back to previous routing on error-rate or latency SLO breach.

5) Safety: keep original routing code path always available; telemetry must include sampling of raw traces for root-cause debugging and a metric for hint-induced correctness regressions (should be zero).
experiment_plan: Stage 0 (unit & integration): implement router and plumbing behind feature flag; run unit and integ tests with synthetic sequences
Stage 1 (canary, 0.5% traffic): enable kernel hint probes and routing decisions for a small set of non-critical tenants; collect 48h baseline
Stage 2 (10% traffic): enable adaptive router for geo-limited cluster; validate latency metrics and per-tenant drilldowns; run adversarial bursts
Stage 3 (50% traffic): expand to mixed-tenancy production cluster with staggered rollouts; monitor cost delta and error signals
Stage 4 (global rollout): gated by telemetry, release to all hosted and dedicated fleets with gradual ramp and post-rollout review
risk_and_mitigation: Risks: (A) Hinting misroutes could cause correctness regressions; mitigation: probe only and strict correctness assertions with immediate rollback on any non-zero regression. (B) Router oscillation — flipping decisions rapidly for borderline fingerprints; mitigation: smoothing window with EWMA and minimum decision duration. (C) Increased resource use from probes; mitigation: cap probe traffic and telemetry sampling. (D) Latency regressions for cold tenants; mitigation: staged rollouts and tenant whitelisting.
rollback_plan: Feature flag off will immediately route traffic to the original ingress path; we will have a 2-minute automated rollback if error rate or p99 increases beyond thresholds. Manual rollback instructions: (1) flip router FF to 'off' in control plane; (2) scale down slowpath workers by 50% to drain; (3) revert kernel hinting commits if toggling flags is insufficient; (4) escalate to on-call infra if rollback does not restore baseline within 10 minutes.

notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on ingress-side mitigations rather than changing model runtimes. If kernel experiments show consistent wins we will open a follow-up ticket to fold hints into the executor scheduling logic.
